audit_status.review_note: Reviewed for Rachel/Leah rivalry, Bilhah/Zilpah birth naming wordplays, mandrakes, Joseph naming, Jacob/Laban wage negotiation, and flock-breeding narrative.

verses.restored: Rachel saw that she had borne Jacob no children, and Rachel envied her sister. She said to Jacob, Give me children, or I am dead.

familiar.text: And when Rachel saw that she bare Jacob no children, Rachel envied her sister...

notes.title: Give me children
notes.body: Rachel’s anguish echoes the recurring barrenness theme, now inside a divided household.

modern.text: When Rachel saw that she was not bearing any children for Jacob, she envied her sister. “Give me children, or I will die!” she said to Jacob.

original.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא רָחֵ֗ל כִּ֣י לֹ֤א יָֽלְדָה֙ לְיַעֲקֹ֔ב וַתְּקַנֵּ֥א רָחֵ֖ל בַּאֲחֹתָ֑הּ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר אֶֽל יַעֲקֹב֙ הָֽבָה לִּ֣י בָנִ֔ים וְאִם אַ֖יִן מֵתָ֥ה אָנֹֽכִי

verses.restored: Jacob’s anger burned against Rachel, and he said, Am I in the place of the Divine, who has withheld from you fruit of the womb?

familiar.text: And Jacob's anger was kindled against Rachel...

modern.text: Jacob became angry with Rachel and said, “Am I in the place of God, who has withheld children from you?”

original.text: וַיִּֽחַר אַ֥ף יַעֲקֹ֖ב בְּרָחֵ֑ל וַיֹּ֗אמֶר הֲתַ֤חַת אֱלֹהִים֙ אָנֹ֔כִי אֲשֶׁר מָנַ֥ע מִמֵּ֖ךְ פְּרִי בָֽטֶן

verses.restored: She said, Look, my slave-woman Bilhah. Go in to her, and she shall bear on my knees, so that I too may be built up through her.

familiar.text: And she said, Behold my maid Bilhah, go in unto her...

notes.title: Built up through her
notes.body: Rachel repeats the household-surrogacy logic previously seen with Sarah and Hagar.

modern.text: Then she said, “Here is my maidservant Bilhah. Sleep with her, that she may bear children for me, so that through her I too can build a family.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֕אמֶר הִנֵּ֛ה אֲמָתִ֥י בִלְהָ֖ה בֹּ֣א אֵלֶ֑יהָ וְתֵלֵד֙ עַל בִּרְכַּ֔י וְאִבָּנֶ֥ה גַם אָנֹכִ֖י מִמֶּֽנָּה

verses.restored: She gave him Bilhah her slave-woman as a woman, and Jacob went in to her.

familiar.text: And she gave him Bilhah her handmaid to wife...

modern.text: So Rachel gave Jacob her servant Bilhah as a wife, and he slept with her,

original.text: וַתִּתֶּן ל֛וֹ אֶת בִּלְהָ֥ה שִׁפְחָתָ֖הּ לְאִשָּׁ֑ה וַיָּבֹ֥א אֵלֶ֖יהָ יַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Bilhah conceived and bore Jacob a son.

familiar.text: And Bilhah conceived, and bare Jacob a son.

modern.text: and Bilhah conceived and bore him a son.

original.text: וַתַּ֣הַר בִּלְהָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּֽן

verses.restored: Rachel said, The Divine has judged me, and has also heard my voice and given me a son. Therefore she called his name Dan.

familiar.text: And Rachel said, God hath judged me...

modern.text: Then Rachel said, “God has vindicated me; He has heard my plea and given me a son.” So she named him Dan.

original.text: וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ דָּנַ֣נִּי אֱלֹהִ֔ים וְגַם֙ שָׁמַ֣ע בְּקֹלִ֔י וַיִּתֶּן לִ֖י בֵּ֑ן עַל כֵּ֛ן קָרְאָ֥ה שְׁמ֖וֹ דָּֽן

verses.restored: Bilhah, Rachel’s slave-woman, conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

familiar.text: And Bilhah Rachel's maid conceived again...

modern.text: And Rachel’s servant Bilhah conceived again and bore Jacob a second son.

original.text: וַתַּ֣הַר ע֔וֹד וַתֵּ֕לֶד בִּלְהָ֖ה שִׁפְחַ֣ת רָחֵ֑ל בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Rachel said, With mighty wrestlings I have wrestled with my sister, and I have prevailed. She called his name Naphtali.

familiar.text: And Rachel said, With great wrestlings have I wrestled with my sister...

modern.text: Then Rachel said, “In my great struggles, I have wrestled with my sister and won.” So she named him Naphtali. Gad and Asher

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל נַפְתּוּלֵ֨י אֱלֹהִ֧ים נִפְתַּ֛לְתִּי עִם אֲחֹתִ֖י גַּם יָכֹ֑לְתִּי וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ נַפְתָּלִֽי

verses.restored: Leah saw that she had stopped bearing, so she took Zilpah her slave-woman and gave her to Jacob as a woman.

familiar.text: When Leah saw that she had left bearing, she took Zilpah...

modern.text: When Leah saw that she had stopped having children, she gave her servant Zilpah to Jacob as a wife.

original.text: וַתֵּ֣רֶא לֵאָ֔ה כִּ֥י עָמְדָ֖ה מִלֶּ֑דֶת וַתִּקַּח֙ אֶת זִלְפָּ֣ה שִׁפְחָתָ֔הּ וַתִּתֵּ֥ן אֹתָ֛הּ לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב לְאִשָּֽׁה

verses.restored: Zilpah, Leah’s slave-woman, bore Jacob a son.

familiar.text: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a son.

modern.text: And Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a son.

original.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּ֛ה שִׁפְחַ֥ת לֵאָ֖ה לְיַעֲקֹ֥ב בֵּֽן

verses.restored: Leah said, Fortune has come! She called his name Gad.

familiar.text: And Leah said, A troop cometh: and she called his name Gad.

notes.title: Gad
notes.body: The name is associated with fortune/troop; the wording is textually and lexically debated.

modern.text: Then Leah said, “How fortunate!” So she named him Gad.

original.text: וַתֹּ֥אמֶר לֵאָ֖ה בגד וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ גָּֽד

verses.restored: Zilpah, Leah’s slave-woman, bore Jacob a second son.

familiar.text: And Zilpah Leah's maid bare Jacob a second son.

modern.text: When Leah’s servant Zilpah bore Jacob a second son,

original.text: וַתֵּ֗לֶד זִלְפָּה֙ שִׁפְחַ֣ת לֵאָ֔ה בֵּ֥ן שֵׁנִ֖י לְיַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Leah said, In my happiness, for daughters will call me happy. She called his name Asher.

familiar.text: And Leah said, Happy am I, for the daughters will call me blessed...

modern.text: Leah said, “How happy I am! For the women call me happy.” So she named him Asher.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֔ה בְּאָשְׁרִ֕י כִּ֥י אִשְּׁר֖וּנִי בָּנ֑וֹת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ אָשֵֽׁר

verses.restored: Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest and found mandrakes in the field, and brought them to Leah his mother. Rachel said to Leah, Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.

familiar.text: And Reuben went in the days of wheat harvest, and found mandrakes...

notes.title: Mandrakes
notes.body: Dudaim were associated with fertility/sexual desire in the ancient world.

modern.text: Now during the wheat harvest, Reuben went out and found some mandrakes in the field. When he brought them to his mother, Rachel begged Leah, “Please give me some of your son’s mandrakes.”

original.text: וַיֵּ֨לֶךְ רְאוּבֵ֜ן בִּימֵ֣י קְצִיר חִטִּ֗ים וַיִּמְצָ֤א דֽוּדָאִים֙ בַּשָּׂדֶ֔ה וַיָּבֵ֣א אֹתָ֔ם אֶל לֵאָ֖ה אִמּ֑וֹ וַתֹּ֤אמֶר רָחֵל֙ אֶל לֵאָ֔ה תְּנִי נָ֣א לִ֔י מִדּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנֵֽךְ

verses.restored: She said to her, Is it a small thing that you have taken my man? Would you also take my son’s mandrakes? Rachel said, Therefore he shall lie with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.

familiar.text: And she said unto her, Is it a small matter that thou hast taken my husband?...

modern.text: But Leah replied, “Is it not enough that you have taken away my husband? Now you want to take my son’s mandrakes as well?” “Very well,” said Rachel, “he may sleep with you tonight in exchange for your son’s mandrakes.”

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לָ֗הּ הַמְעַט֙ קַחְתֵּ֣ךְ אֶת אִישִׁ֔י וְלָקַ֕חַת גַּ֥ם אֶת דּוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַתֹּ֣אמֶר רָחֵ֗ל לָכֵן֙ יִשְׁכַּ֤ב עִמָּךְ֙ הַלַּ֔יְלָה תַּ֖חַת דּוּדָאֵ֥י בְנֵֽךְ

verses.restored: Jacob came from the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him and said, You must come in to me, for I have surely hired you with my son’s mandrakes. So he lay with her that night.

familiar.text: And Jacob came out of the field in the evening, and Leah went out to meet him...

modern.text: When Jacob came in from the field that evening, Leah went out to meet him and said, “You must come with me, for I have hired you with my son’s mandrakes.” So he slept with her that night. Issachar, Zebulun, and Dinah

original.text: וַיָּבֹ֨א יַעֲקֹ֣ב מִן הַשָּׂדֶה֮ בָּעֶרֶב֒ וַתֵּצֵ֨א לֵאָ֜ה לִקְרָאת֗וֹ וַתֹּ֨אמֶר֙ אֵלַ֣י תָּב֔וֹא כִּ֚י שָׂכֹ֣ר שְׂכַרְתִּ֔יךָ בְּדוּדָאֵ֖י בְּנִ֑י וַיִּשְׁכַּ֥ב עִמָּ֖הּ בַּלַּ֥יְלָה הֽוּא

verses.restored: The Divine listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore Jacob a fifth son.

familiar.text: And God hearkened unto Leah, and she conceived...

modern.text: And God listened to Leah, and she conceived and bore a fifth son to Jacob.

original.text: וַיִּשְׁמַ֥ע אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶל לֵאָ֑ה וַתַּ֛הַר וַתֵּ֥לֶד לְיַעֲקֹ֖ב בֵּ֥ן חֲמִישִֽׁי

verses.restored: Leah said, The Divine has given me my wages, because I gave my slave-woman to my man. She called his name Issachar.

familiar.text: And Leah said, God hath given me my hire...

modern.text: Then Leah said, “God has rewarded me for giving my maidservant to my husband.” So she named him Issachar.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה נָתַ֤ן אֱלֹהִים֙ שְׂכָרִ֔י אֲשֶׁר נָתַ֥תִּי שִׁפְחָתִ֖י לְאִישִׁ֑י וַתִּקְרָ֥א שְׁמ֖וֹ יִשָּׂשכָֽר

verses.restored: Leah conceived again and bore Jacob a sixth son.

familiar.text: And Leah conceived again, and bare Jacob the sixth son.

modern.text: Again Leah conceived and bore a sixth son to Jacob.

original.text: וַתַּ֤הַר עוֹד֙ לֵאָ֔ה וַתֵּ֥לֶד בֵּן שִׁשִּׁ֖י לְּיַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: Leah said, The Divine has endowed me with a good endowment; this time my man will honor/dwell with me, because I have borne him six sons. She called his name Zebulun.

familiar.text: And Leah said, God hath endued me with a good dowry...

notes.title: Zebulun
notes.body: The name is linked with endowment/honor/dwelling wordplay.

modern.text: “God has given me a good gift,” she said. “This time my husband will honor me, because I have borne him six sons.” And she named him Zebulun.

original.text: וַתֹּ֣אמֶר לֵאָ֗ה זְבָדַ֨נִי אֱלֹהִ֥ים אֹתִי֮ זֵ֣בֶד טוֹב֒ הַפַּ֨עַם֙ יִזְבְּלֵ֣נִי אִישִׁ֔י כִּֽי יָלַ֥דְתִּי ל֖וֹ שִׁשָּׁ֣ה בָנִ֑ים וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמ֖וֹ זְבֻלֽוּן

verses.restored: Afterward she bore a daughter and called her name Dinah.

familiar.text: And afterwards she bare a daughter, and called her name Dinah.

modern.text: After that, Leah gave birth to a daughter and named her Dinah. Joseph

original.text: וְאַחַ֖ר יָ֣לְדָה בַּ֑ת וַתִּקְרָ֥א אֶת שְׁמָ֖הּ דִּינָֽה

verses.restored: The Divine remembered Rachel, and the Divine listened to her and opened her womb.

familiar.text: And God remembered Rachel, and God hearkened to her, and opened her womb.

notes.title: Remembered Rachel
notes.body: Divine remembering means covenantal attention and action.

modern.text: Then God remembered Rachel. He listened to her and opened her womb,

original.text: וַיִּזְכֹּ֥ר אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת רָחֵ֑ל וַיִּשְׁמַ֤ע אֵלֶ֨יהָ֙ אֱלֹהִ֔ים וַיִּפְתַּ֖ח אֶת רַחְמָֽהּ

verses.restored: She conceived and bore a son, and said, The Divine has gathered away my disgrace.

familiar.text: And she conceived, and bare a son; and said, God hath taken away my reproach:

modern.text: and she conceived and gave birth to a son. “God has taken away my shame,” she said.

original.text: וַתַּ֖הַר וַתֵּ֣לֶד בֵּ֑ן וַתֹּ֕אמֶר אָסַ֥ף אֱלֹהִ֖ים אֶת חֶרְפָּתִֽי

verses.restored: She called his name Joseph, saying, May the Eternal add to me another son.

familiar.text: And she called his name Joseph; and said, The LORD shall add to me another son.

notes.title: Joseph
notes.body: Joseph is linked with gathering away and adding.

modern.text: She named him Joseph, and said, “May the LORD add to me another son.” Jacob Prospers

original.text: וַתִּקְרָ֧א אֶת שְׁמ֛וֹ יוֹסֵ֖ף לֵאמֹ֑ר יֹסֵ֧ף יְהוָ֛ה לִ֖י בֵּ֥ן אַחֵֽר

verses.restored: After Rachel had borne Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, Send me away, so I may go to my place and to my land.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, when Rachel had born Joseph, that Jacob said unto Laban...

modern.text: Now after Rachel had given birth to Joseph, Jacob said to Laban, “Send me on my way so I can return to my homeland.

original.text: וַיְהִ֕י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר יָלְדָ֥ה רָחֵ֖ל אֶת יוֹסֵ֑ף וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ אֶל לָבָ֔ן שַׁלְּחֵ֨נִי֙ וְאֵ֣לְכָ֔ה אֶל מְקוֹמִ֖י וּלְאַרְצִֽי

verses.restored: Give me my women and my children for whom I have served you, and let me go, for you know my service that I have served you.

familiar.text: Give me my wives and my children, for whom I have served thee...

modern.text: Give me my wives and children for whom I have served you, that I may go on my way. You know how hard I have worked for you.”

original.text: תְּנָ֞ה אֶת נָשַׁ֣י וְאֶת יְלָדַ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר עָבַ֧דְתִּי אֹֽתְךָ֛ בָּהֵ֖ן וְאֵלֵ֑כָה כִּ֚י אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֶת עֲבֹדָתִ֖י אֲשֶׁ֥ר עֲבַדְתִּֽיךָ

verses.restored: Laban said to him, If now I have found favor in your eyes, I have divined that the Eternal has blessed me because of you.

familiar.text: And Laban said unto him, I pray thee, if I have found favour...

notes.title: Divined
notes.body: Nichashti can mean I have learned by divination/observation. Laban attributes his prosperity to Jacob.

modern.text: But Laban replied, “If I have found favor in your eyes, please stay. I have learned by divination that the LORD has blessed me because of you.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֤אמֶר אֵלָיו֙ לָבָ֔ן אִם נָ֛א מָצָ֥אתִי חֵ֖ן בְּעֵינֶ֑יךָ נִחַ֕שְׁתִּי וַיְבָרֲכֵ֥נִי יְהוָ֖ה בִּגְלָלֶֽךָ

verses.restored: He said, Name your wages to me, and I will give it.

familiar.text: And he said, Appoint me thy wages, and I will give it.

modern.text: And he added, “Name your wages, and I will pay them.”

original.text: וַיֹּאמַ֑ר נָקְבָ֧ה שְׂכָרְךָ֛ עָלַ֖י וְאֶתֵּֽנָה

verses.restored: He said to him, You know how I have served you and how your livestock has been with me.

familiar.text: And he said unto him, Thou knowest how I have served thee...

modern.text: Then Jacob answered, “You know how I have served you and how your livestock have thrived under my care.

original.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר אֵלָ֔יו אַתָּ֣ה יָדַ֔עְתָּ אֵ֖ת אֲשֶׁ֣ר עֲבַדְתִּ֑יךָ וְאֵ֛ת אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֥ה מִקְנְךָ֖ אִתִּֽי

verses.restored: For the little you had before me has burst forth into abundance, and the Eternal has blessed you at my foot. Now when shall I also provide for my own house?

familiar.text: For it was little which thou hadst before I came, and it is now increased...

modern.text: Indeed, you had very little before my arrival, but now your wealth has increased many times over. The LORD has blessed you wherever I set foot. But now, when may I also provide for my own household?”

original.text: כִּ֡י מְעַט֩ אֲשֶׁר הָיָ֨ה לְךָ֤ לְפָנַי֙ וַיִּפְרֹ֣ץ לָרֹ֔ב וַיְבָ֧רֶךְ יְהוָ֛ה אֹתְךָ֖ לְרַגְלִ֑י וְעַתָּ֗ה מָתַ֛י אֶֽעֱשֶׂ֥ה גַם אָנֹכִ֖י לְבֵיתִֽי

verses.restored: He said, What shall I give you? Jacob said, You shall not give me anything. If you will do this thing for me, I will return, pasture your flock, and keep it.

familiar.text: And he said, What shall I give thee? And Jacob said, Thou shalt not give me any thing...

modern.text: “What can I give you?” Laban asked. “You do not need to give me anything,” Jacob replied. “If you do this one thing for me, I will keep on shepherding and keeping your flocks.

original.text: וַיֹּ֖אמֶר מָ֣ה אֶתֶּן לָ֑ךְ וַיֹּ֤אמֶר יַעֲקֹב֙ לֹא תִתֶּן לִ֣י מְא֔וּמָה אִם תַּֽעֲשֶׂה לִּי֙ הַדָּבָ֣ר הַזֶּ֔ה אָשׁ֛וּבָה אֶרְעֶ֥ה צֹֽאנְךָ֖ אֶשְׁמֹֽר

verses.restored: Let me pass through all your flock today, removing from there every speckled and spotted sheep, every dark one among the lambs, and the spotted and speckled among the goats; these shall be my wages.

familiar.text: I will pass through all thy flock to day, removing from thence all the speckled...

modern.text: Let me go through all your flocks today and remove from them every speckled or spotted sheep, every dark-colored lamb, and every spotted or speckled goat. These will be my wages.

original.text: אֶֽעֱבֹ֨ר בְּכָל צֹֽאנְךָ֜ הַיּ֗וֹם הָסֵ֨ר מִשָּׁ֜ם כָּל שֶׂ֣ה נָקֹ֣ד וְטָל֗וּא וְכָל שֶׂה חוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים וְטָל֥וּא וְנָקֹ֖ד בָּעִזִּ֑ים וְהָיָ֖ה שְׂכָרִֽי

verses.restored: My righteousness will answer for me in a later day, when you come concerning my wages before you: every one that is not speckled or spotted among the goats, or dark among the lambs, shall be counted stolen with me.

familiar.text: So shall my righteousness answer for me in time to come...

modern.text: So my honesty will testify for me when you come to check on my wages in the future. If I have any goats that are not speckled or spotted, or any lambs that are not dark-colored, they will be considered stolen.”

original.text: וְעָֽנְתָה בִּ֤י צִדְקָתִי֙ בְּי֣וֹם מָחָ֔ר כִּֽי תָב֥וֹא עַל שְׂכָרִ֖י לְפָנֶ֑יךָ כֹּ֣ל אֲשֶׁר אֵינֶנּוּ֩ נָקֹ֨ד וְטָל֜וּא בָּֽעִזִּ֗ים וְחוּם֙ בַּכְּשָׂבִ֔ים גָּנ֥וּב ה֖וּא אִתִּֽי

verses.restored: Laban said, Look, let it be according to your word.

familiar.text: And Laban said, Behold, I would it might be according to thy word.

modern.text: “Agreed,” said Laban. “Let it be as you have said.”

original.text: וַיֹּ֥אמֶר לָבָ֖ן הֵ֑ן ל֖וּ יְהִ֥י כִדְבָרֶֽךָ

verses.restored: That day he removed the striped and spotted male goats, all the speckled and spotted female goats, every one that had white in it, and every dark one among the lambs, and put them in the hand of his sons.

familiar.text: And he removed that day the he goats that were ringstraked and spotted...

modern.text: That very day Laban removed all the streaked or spotted male goats and every speckled or spotted female goat—every one that had any white on it—and every dark-colored lamb, and he placed them under the care of his sons.

original.text: וַיָּ֣סַר בַּיּוֹם֩ הַה֨וּא אֶת הַתְּיָשִׁ֜ים הָֽעֲקֻדִּ֣ים וְהַטְּלֻאִ֗ים וְאֵ֤ת כָּל הָֽעִזִּים֙ הַנְּקֻדּ֣וֹת וְהַטְּלֻאֹ֔ת כֹּ֤ל אֲשֶׁר לָבָן֙ בּ֔וֹ וְכָל ח֖וּם בַּכְּשָׂבִ֑ים וַיִּתֵּ֖ן בְּיַד בָּנָֽיו

verses.restored: He set a distance of three days’ journey between himself and Jacob, and Jacob pastured the rest of Laban’s flock.

familiar.text: And he set three days' journey betwixt himself and Jacob...

modern.text: Then he put a three-day journey between himself and Jacob, while Jacob was shepherding the rest of Laban’s flocks.

original.text: וַיָּ֗שֶׂם דֶּ֚רֶךְ שְׁלֹ֣שֶׁת יָמִ֔ים בֵּינ֖וֹ וּבֵ֣ין יַעֲקֹ֑ב וְיַעֲקֹ֗ב רֹעֶ֛ה אֶת צֹ֥אן לָבָ֖ן הַנּוֹתָרֹֽת

verses.restored: Jacob took fresh rods of poplar, almond, and plane tree, peeled white streaks in them, exposing the white on the rods.

familiar.text: And Jacob took him rods of green poplar, and of the hazel and chesnut tree...

notes.title: Rods and streaks
notes.body: The flock-breeding method reflects ancient observation/practice, not modern genetics.

modern.text: Jacob, however, took fresh branches of poplar, almond, and plane trees, and peeled the bark, exposing the white inner wood of the branches.

original.text: וַיִּֽקַּֽח ל֣וֹ יַעֲקֹ֗ב מַקַּ֥ל לִבְנֶ֛ה לַ֖ח וְל֣וּז וְעֶרְמ֑וֹן וַיְפַצֵּ֤ל בָּהֵן֙ פְּצָל֣וֹת לְבָנ֔וֹת מַחְשֹׂף֙ הַלָּבָ֔ן אֲשֶׁ֖ר עַל הַמַּקְלֽוֹת

verses.restored: He set the rods he had peeled in front of the flocks, in the troughs, in the watering places where the flocks came to drink, and they bred when they came to drink.

familiar.text: And he set the rods which he had pilled before the flocks...

modern.text: Then he set the peeled branches in the watering troughs in front of the flocks coming in to drink. So when the flocks were in heat and came to drink,

original.text: וַיַּצֵּ֗ג אֶת הַמַּקְלוֹת֙ אֲשֶׁ֣ר פִּצֵּ֔ל בָּרֳהָטִ֖ים בְּשִֽׁקֲת֣וֹת הַמָּ֑יִם אֲשֶׁר֩ תָּבֹ֨אןָ הַצֹּ֤אן לִשְׁתּוֹת֙ לְנֹ֣כַח הַצֹּ֔אן וַיֵּחַ֖מְנָה בְּבֹאָ֥ן לִשְׁתּֽוֹת

verses.restored: The flocks bred by the rods, and the flocks brought forth striped, speckled, and spotted.

familiar.text: And the flocks conceived before the rods, and brought forth cattle ringstraked...

modern.text: they mated in front of the branches. And they bore young that were streaked or speckled or spotted.

original.text: וַיֶּחֱמ֥וּ הַצֹּ֖אן אֶל הַמַּקְל֑וֹת וַתֵּלַ֣דְןָ הַצֹּ֔אן עֲקֻדִּ֥ים נְקֻדִּ֖ים וּטְלֻאִֽים

verses.restored: Jacob separated the lambs and set the faces of the flock toward the striped and all the dark in Laban’s flock. He put his own droves apart and did not put them with Laban’s flock.

familiar.text: And Jacob did separate the lambs, and set the faces of the flocks...

modern.text: Jacob set apart the young, but made the rest face the streaked dark-colored sheep in Laban’s flocks. Then he set his own stock apart and did not put them with Laban’s animals.

original.text: וְהַכְּשָׂבִים֮ הִפְרִ֣יד יַעֲקֹב֒ וַ֠יִּתֵּן פְּנֵ֨י הַצֹּ֧אן אֶל עָקֹ֛ד וְכָל ח֖וּם בְּצֹ֣אן לָבָ֑ן וַיָּֽשֶׁת ל֤וֹ עֲדָרִים֙ לְבַדּ֔וֹ וְלֹ֥א שָׁתָ֖ם עַל צֹ֥אן לָבָֽן

verses.restored: Whenever the strong of the flock were breeding, Jacob put the rods before the eyes of the flock in the troughs, so that they might breed among the rods.

familiar.text: And it came to pass, whensoever the stronger cattle did conceive...

modern.text: Whenever the stronger females of the flock were in heat, Jacob would place the branches in the troughs, in full view of the animals, so that they would breed in front of the branches.

original.text: וְהָיָ֗ה בְּכָל יַחֵם֮ הַצֹּ֣אן הַמְקֻשָּׁרוֹת֒ וְשָׂ֨ם יַעֲקֹ֧ב אֶת הַמַּקְל֛וֹת לְעֵינֵ֥י הַצֹּ֖אן בָּרֳהָטִ֑ים לְיַחְמֵ֖נָּה בַּמַּקְלֽוֹת

verses.restored: But when the flock was weak, he did not put them in. So the weak were Laban’s, and the strong were Jacob’s.

familiar.text: But when the cattle were feeble, he put them not in...

modern.text: But if the animals were weak, he did not set out the branches. So the weaker animals went to Laban and the stronger ones to Jacob.

original.text: וּבְהַעֲטִ֥יף הַצֹּ֖אן לֹ֣א יָשִׂ֑ים וְהָיָ֤ה הָעֲטֻפִים֙ לְלָבָ֔ן וְהַקְּשֻׁרִ֖ים לְיַעֲקֹֽב

verses.restored: The man broke forth exceedingly, and he had many flocks, female servants, male servants, camels, and donkeys.

familiar.text: And the man increased exceedingly, and had much cattle...

modern.text: Thus Jacob became exceedingly prosperous. He owned large flocks, maidservants and menservants, and camels and donkeys.

original.text: וַיִּפְרֹ֥ץ הָאִ֖ישׁ מְאֹ֣ד מְאֹ֑ד וַֽיְהִי לוֹ֙ צֹ֣אן רַבּ֔וֹת וּשְׁפָחוֹת֙ וַעֲבָדִ֔ים וּגְמַלִּ֖ים וַחֲמֹרִֽים
